sequence_description: Direct-endpoint attack: attempt to inject authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) against a public client.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization endpoint appears to accept an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) for a public client, which can enable parameter injection if request object contents are honored.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization endpoint appears to accept an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) for a public client, which can enable parameter injection if request object contents are honored.

sequence_description: Direct endpoint (OIDC auth): attempt request_uri injection where the referenced request object is unsigned (alg=none). Auth endpoint should not accept an unsigned request object via request_uri indirection.
description: [LLM-Judge] The platform appears to accept a request object fetched via request_uri even when it is unsigned (alg=none), which should be rejected to prevent request_uri/request object injection.

evidence.llm_judge_description: The platform appears to accept a request object fetched via request_uri even when it is unsigned (alg=none), which should be rejected to prevent request_uri/request object injection.

sequence_description: I4 cross_protocol_identity_merge: Local password user exists, then brokered SAML login uses same email but different upstream NameID; verify Keycloak does not merge into the existing local user when auto-linking/trust-email is disabled.
description: [LLM-Judge] Test could not execute the intended cross-protocol identity-merge check because client creation failed, causing all subsequent logins to fail with invalid_client.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Test could not execute the intended cross-protocol identity-merge check because client creation failed, causing all subsequent logins to fail with invalid_client.

sequence_description: I5: Use an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) to attempt scope escalation at the authorization endpoint. If accepted, attacker can inject broader scopes/claims than intended by client policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none), which can enable parameter/scope injection if request objects are expected to be signed/enforced.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none), which can enable parameter/scope injection if request objects are expected to be signed/enforced.

sequence_description: I5: Request-object integrity + scope escalation after admin config change. First, verify alg=none request object is rejected (secure baseline). Then weaken client policy by leaving request object signature algorithm unset and retry alg=none to see if unsigned request object can inject broader scope than intended.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned (alg=none) request object appears to be accepted both before and after the attempted policy change, contradicting the test’s secure-baseline expectation and suggesting request-object signature enforcement may be missing or the test is not actually exercising the intended client/policy.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unsigned (alg=none) request object appears to be accepted both before and after the attempted policy change, contradicting the test’s secure-baseline expectation and suggesting request-object signature enforcement may be missing or the test is not actually exercising the intended client/policy.
